intro: G3-PLC and PRIME send data over the low-voltage power cables themselves, from a data concentrator at the transformer to every electricity meter on its feeders. Both use OFDM (many carriers at once) between about 35 and 91 kHz, the CENELEC A band in Europe. A meter that cannot hear the concentrator talks through its neighbours. G3-PLC builds a mesh and carries IPv6, squeezed by 6LoWPAN, with DLMS/COSEM on top. PRIME builds a tree instead, some meters acting as switches for others, and usually carries DLMS/COSEM without IPv6. Together they read tens of millions of meters in Europe.
plain: The power cable that brings electricity to every house can carry messages too, like a whisper riding on the wire. A box next to the neighbourhood transformer talks to every electricity meter this way. A meter too far away to be heard hands its messages to a neighbour, who passes them on, like buckets along a chain. That is how meters are read every day without anyone visiting.

join.title: Join the network
join.text: A new meter, M2, is installed at the end of the street. It cannot hear the concentrator directly, only its neighbour M1. It joins through M1: with EAP-PSK, a login with a key put into the meter at the factory, it proves who it is. It gets the network key and a short address, 0x0002.

route.title: Find a way
route.text: To reach M2, the concentrator floods a route request through the meters with LOADng, a routing protocol for small devices. M2 answers along the cheapest path, through M1. Each meter on the way notes the next hop: the meters build the mesh themselves.

read.title: Read the meter
read.text: The concentrator asks M2 for its energy register 1-0:1.8.0 with a DLMS/COSEM GET. It travels in an IPv6 packet that 6LoWPAN squeezes from 48 bytes of headers to 9. A mesh header says: from 0x0000 to 0x0002. M1 hears it on the cable and passes it on.

answer.title: The answer comes back
answer.text: M2 answers the same way, from 0x0002 to 0x0000, through M1: 303603, in tens of watt-hours, so 3036.03 kWh. On the cable, the MAC layer also encrypts each hop with the network key and adds a CRC.

upload.title: Send it on
upload.text: Every hour or every night, the concentrator sends the readings of all its meters to the head-end system, the utility's metering server, over cellular or fibre.

frames.join: I am meter M2: here is my proof
frames.accepted: Welcome: you are 0x0002, here is the network key
frames.get: M2, what does your energy register say?

notes.discover: M2 sends a beacon request on the cable. Every node that hears it answers with a beacon that gives its route cost to the concentrator. M2 picks M1, the cheapest, as the neighbour that will relay its joining.
notes.join: The LoWPAN Bootstrapping Protocol (LBP) carries an EAP-PSK exchange, relayed by M1. Its four messages prove that M2 and the concentrator know M2's pre-shared key, without sending the key itself.
notes.accepted: At the end of the exchange, protected by the session key, M2 receives the network key (GMK) and its short address 0x0002. LBP ACCEPTED closes the joining.
notes.rreq: A LOADng route request for 0x0002, flooded: every meter that hears it adds the cost of the link it came over and sends it on once.
notes.rrep: M2 answers along the cheapest path, hop by hop: through M1. Each node on the way records the next hop towards 0x0002 and towards 0x0000.
notes.upload: Not G3-PLC: the concentrator sends the day's readings to the head-end over cellular or fibre, often as a file through a web service, or with DLMS/COSEM over TCP (see the DLMS/COSEM lesson).

mesh.name: Mesh header
mesh.note: 0xB8 = 10 1 1 1000: a mesh header (10), both addresses short (1, 1), hops left 8. M1 lowers it to 7 when it passes the frame on.

mesh-dc-m2.name: Originator · final destination
mesh-dc-m2.note: 0x0000, the concentrator, to 0x0002, meter M2. The MAC header in front names only the next hop, M1.

mesh-m2-dc.name: Originator · final destination
mesh-m2-dc.note: 0x0002 to 0x0000: from M2 back to the concentrator.

iphc.name: IPHC
iphc.note: 0x7E33: a compressed IPv6 header (RFC 6282). Traffic class and flow label left out, next header compressed, hop limit 64, and both addresses rebuilt from the mesh header: 40 bytes of IPv6 in 2.

nhc-udp.name: UDP header, compressed
nhc-udp.note: 0xF0: a compressed UDP header follows, with both ports and the checksum in full.

ports.name: Ports
ports.note: 4059 and 4059 (0x0FDB): the DLMS/COSEM port, used at both ends here. The UDP length is left out: it follows from the length of the frame.

checksum-get.name: UDP checksum
checksum-get.note: 0xC190, over the rebuilt IPv6 addresses, the UDP header and the data. The meter checks it.

version.name: Version
version.note: 1: the DLMS/COSEM wrapper, the same as on TCP.

wports-dc.name: wPorts
wports-dc.note: From client 0x0011 to the meter's management logical device 0x0001.

wports-m2.name: wPorts
wports-m2.note: From the meter's logical device 0x0001 back to client 0x0011.

invoke.name: Invoke ID and priority
invoke.note: 0xC1: high priority, confirmed, invoke ID 1. The answer carries the same byte.

class-3.name: Class 3
class-3.note: Register: a value with a scaler and a unit.

raw.name: Value
raw.note: 0x0004A1F3 = 303603. This meter's scaler is ×10 Wh: 3036.03 kWh.

a-prefix.name: fe80::/64
a-prefix.note: The link-local prefix: valid only inside this PLC network.

a-fill.name: 00 FF FE 00
a-fill.note: A fixed filler between the PAN ID and the short address.

a-short.name: Short address
a-short.note: 0x0002: meter M2, the address it got when it joined.

facts.standard: ITU-T G.9903 (G3-PLC) and ITU-T G.9904 (PRIME). G3-PLC carries IPv6 with 6LoWPAN (RFC 4944, RFC 6282) and routes with LOADng
facts.between: A data concentrator at the MV/LV transformer and the electricity meters on its low-voltage feeders
facts.transport: OFDM on the power cable; in Europe the CENELEC A band, about 35 – 91 kHz
facts.security: G3-PLC: each meter joins with EAP-PSK and gets the network key; the MAC layer encrypts with AES-128. DLMS/COSEM adds its own AES-GCM on top
facts.speed: Tens of kbit/s; every hop adds delay, so reading hundreds of meters takes minutes

tips: Noise and loads on the cable change the reach hour by hour: a new inverter or charger can cut meters off. Look at each meter's link quality over days, not at one reading.
Signals cross where cables meet: a meter may join a neighbouring concentrator, behind another transformer. Check which PAN each meter really joined.
Load every meter's pre-shared key into the head-end before installation. Without it, the meter cannot join.
Encrypt at the DLMS/COSEM layer too: the PLC network key is shared by all the meters of a concentrator.

anatomy.address: M2's IPv6 address, rebuilt from the mesh header

playground.file: Try it: the topology a concentrator might export: every meter it has heard of, and how to reach it. The file is made up; every make of concentrator has its own format.
playground.columns: The short address, the meter's EUI-64 (its factory address), the next hop, the number of hops, the route cost (lower is better), the link quality (higher is better) and the phase.
playground.direct: M1 is its own next hop: the concentrator hears it directly.
playground.relayed: M2 is reached through 0x0001, meter M1, in 2 hops: a higher cost and a weaker link.
playground.phase: This meter hangs on phase L2. G3-PLC can tell the phase from when each frame arrives against the mains cycle.
playground.far: 3 hops away, with the weakest link: the first meter to drop out when the cable gets noisy.
